claim.pdf_says: SORT Format 2 (table), COLLATING SEQUENCE clause. The printed figure is an outer BRACKET containing 'COLLATING SEQUENCE' followed by a BRACE with two alternatives: alternative 1 = 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]'; alternative 2 = an inner BRACE WITH CHOICE INDICATORS, i.e. a vertical bar just inside each side of the inner brace, spanning the two lines 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2'. Rendered linearly: [ COLLATING SEQUENCE { IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ] | { | FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 | / | FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 | } } ]
claim.why_it_matters: Two separate losses, both toward falsely-restrictive syntax. (1) The choice-indicator bars just inside the inner brace are gone; per 5.2.6.4 those bars mean the enclosed alternatives may each be specified at most once, in any order, so 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1' and 'FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2' may BOTH appear. Without the bars the markdown reads as select-exactly-one, making a legal table SORT that sets both an alphanumeric and a national collating sequence look illegal. (2) The nesting is garbled: 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' is shown inside the same inner brace as the two FOR lines, whereas the PDF makes it a sibling ALTERNATIVE to the whole bar-group. The identical construct in SORT Format 1 (page 775) has already been repaired in the markdown with box-drawing brackets plus a 'Figure notes (SORT Format 1)' paragraph; Format 2 was left unrepaired, so the two general formats of the same statement now contradict each other.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED by direct inspection of the rendered page at 300 dpi, magnified 5-6x on both sides of the COLLATING SEQUENCE figure (E:/Temp/specrecon/v776/spec_p776.png, crops crop_collating.png, crop_left2.png, crop_right_inner.png).

WHAT I SEE IN THE PRINTED GLYPHS. Left side, scanning left to right after 'COLLATING SEQUENCE': (1) a tall opening curly brace spanning all three text lines; (2) a shorter opening curly brace spanning ONLY the two FOR lines; (3) a straight, unadorned VERTICAL BAR spanning only the two FOR lines, standing just inside that shorter brace; then 'FOR ALPHANUMERIC ...' / 'FOR NATIONAL ...'. Right side, scanning right to left: (1) a tall square bracket ']'; (2) a tall closing curly brace spanning all three lines; (3) a shorter closing curly brace spanning only the two FOR lines; (4) a straight VERTICAL BAR spanning only the two FOR lines, just inside that shorter brace. The two bars are plainly straight strokes with no hooks or mid-point cusp — unmistakably distinct from the adjacent brace glyphs, which show the characteristic upper hook, middle cusp and lower hook. So a genuine matched pair of choice indicators is printed, enclosed by the inner brace, exactly as 5.2.6.4 requires ('The pair of bars comprising the choice indicator shall be enclosed either by brackets or braces').

NESTING AS PRINTED. The inner brace + bar pair spans ONLY the two FOR lines. The line 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' sits outside it, at the top, directly under the outer brace. The outer brace therefore offers exactly two alternatives: the single-line 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' form, or the bar-group. This is structurally identical to the SORT Format 1 figure on page 775.

WHAT THE MARKDOWN HAS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 14-16 of the page-776 block are quoted verbatim and accurately in the claim. Both bars are absent, and the doubled ASCII braces '{ {' / '} }' span all three rows, so 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' is rendered as a peer of the two FOR lines inside one three-way select-exactly-one brace.

WHY THIS IS NORMATIVE, NOT COSMETIC. 5.2.6.4 (verified in specs/ISO_COBOL.md, section-5-2-6-4): 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. When enclosed by braces, one or more of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative shall be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' The printed figure therefore permits SORT data-name-2 ... COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alpha-1 FOR NATIONAL IS nat-1 (both phrases, either order). The markdown, having lost the bars, permits only one of the three lines — it forbids a construct the standard allows. That is precisely the falsely-restrictive OCR failure mode. Syntax rules 1) and 2) on this same page ('Alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric collating sequence' / 'Alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence') corroborate that both alphabets are meant to be specifiable together.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION CONFIRMED. Page 775 in the markdown already carries the repaired Format 1 figure using box-drawing braces with explicit choice indicators ('⎧|' ... '|⎫') plus a 'Figure notes (SORT Format 1)' paragraph that states in terms: 'that means one or more of the enclosed alternatives shall be specified, each at most once, in any order — so FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 and FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2 may BOTH appear ... It is NOT a select-exactly-one brace.' Format 2 on page 776 was left unrepaired, so the transcription now asserts opposite syntax for the same clause one page apart.

ADVERSARIAL CHECKS THAT FAILED TO REFUTE. The bars are not reflowed onto an adjacent line, not present anywhere else in the page-776 block, and no figure-notes paragraph compensates for their absence (the whole page-776 block is 10 lines; I read it in full). The difference is not line wrapping, hyphenation, or page-break furniture — it is a lost glyph pair plus a changed brace span. The claim does not misquote either source: the markdown is quoted character-for-character, and the PDF prose description matches the printed glyphs. The unrelated parts of the figure (SORT data-name-2, the ON ASCENDING/DESCENDING KEY bracket with 'KEY [ data-name-1 ]', WITH DUPLICATES IN ORDER) are transcribed correctly and are not at issue.
verdict.corrected_description:
The finding is real and the claim's prose description of the PDF is accurate; only the claim's ad-hoc linear rendering is loose and should not be copied into the repair. Two clarifications for whoever lands the fix.

(1) The claim's linear string reuses '|' both as an alternative separator between the two outer-brace alternatives and as the choice-indicator glyph, which is ambiguous. There is exactly ONE pair of tall vertical bars, one on each side, each spanning both FOR lines as a unit — not one bar per line. Use the page-775 convention instead.

(2) The inner brace in the PDF spans ONLY the two FOR lines; the markdown's inner brace wrongly spans all three. Stating the defect as 'nesting garbled' is correct, and the precise form is: the markdown promoted 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' into the bar-group's brace, turning a two-way outer choice (single-line form vs. bar-group) into a three-way select-exactly-one.

RECOMMENDED REPAIR — replace the page-776 COLLATING SEQUENCE lines with the box-drawing form already used for Format 1 on page 775, so the two general formats agree:

  ⎡                      ⎧  IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]     ⎫ ⎤
  ⎢ COLLATING SEQUENCE   ⎨ ⎧| FOR ALPHANUMERIC IS alphabet-name-1 |⎫   ⎬ ⎥
  ⎣                      ⎩ ⎩| FOR NATIONAL IS alphabet-name-2     |⎭   ⎭ ⎦

and append a 'Figure notes (SORT Format 2)' paragraph mirroring the Format 1 note: the second alternative is a brace with choice indicators, so per 5.2.6.4 one or more of the enclosed alternatives shall be specified, each at most once, in any order — FOR ALPHANUMERIC and FOR NATIONAL may BOTH appear, in either order; it is NOT a select-exactly-one brace; the enclosing brace chooses between that bar-group and the single-line 'IS alphabet-name-1 [ alphabet-name-2 ]' form; the whole clause is optional. Required words underlined in the printed Format 2 figure: SORT, ASCENDING, DESCENDING, DUPLICATES, SEQUENCE, ALPHANUMERIC, NATIONAL (COLLATING is not underlined). Note also that Format 2's KEY phrase is bracketed, 'KEY [ data-name-1 ] …', whereas Format 1's is braced, 'KEY { data-name-1 } …'; the markdown already has this right and it must not be 'harmonized' away while repairing the figure.
